title: Forced Index Flows
market_behavior: Index additions, deletions, and reconstitutions can force benchmark-tracking vehicles to trade near predictable windows.
forced_actor: Index funds, ETFs, benchmark-constrained managers, and managers minimizing tracking error.
why_edge_might_exist: Some participants must transact because of index membership changes rather than because the new price is attractive.
why_large_capital_may_ignore_it: Obvious index events are crowded, but smaller events may be operationally messy, capacity-limited, and expensive after spreads and borrow or liquidity costs.
capacity_hypothesis: Capacity is likely event-specific and lower in smaller names; expected personal-capital capacity may be meaningful only where daily dollar volume and spread allow conservative sizing.
observable_predictions: Deletion or addition cohorts show abnormal drift or reversal after announcement/effective windows.
Effects weaken materially after spread, liquidity, and event-date accuracy checks.
falsification_tests: Reject if event returns disappear after realistic spread and liquidity assumptions.
Reject if results depend on using effective dates when announcement dates were required.
Treat as untested until event data provenance is auditable.
references: Academic literature on index reconstitution and price pressure
Index methodology documents and rebalance calendars
